description:
🟡 **iOS compiles but cannot be constructed, let alone run.** The 2026-08-20 pass got `swift build` to zero errors and zero warnings — which proved the code is well-formed, and nothing more.

Three things stand between compiling and running:

- **`UploadStore` is a protocol with no conforming type.** `Store/UploadStore.swift` declares 14 methods — get, leases, resume data, pruning — and no SQLite implementation exists anywhere in the tree. The doc comment already argues *why* SQLite over Core Data; that reasoning is the spec.
- **`AmphoraUploader.swift:27` is a TODO where the graph should be** — *"build the graph — session manager, governors, transport, engine, reconciler."* Nothing wires the parts together.
- **Two `fatalError("unimplemented")` landmines** in `StorageGovernor` — `writeRemainder` (line 62) and the PHAsset export (line 91). `writeRemainder` is on a path `TUSKitTransport:73` already calls, so a resumed upload crashes rather than fails.

**Scope: the simple path only.** Offset-zero, plain-file sources — which is the common case for a first attempt and, deliberately, the path that touches neither `fatalError`. Filling those two is `60`. What this tasklist buys is an uploader you can actually instantiate and send bytes with.

userStories.title: A concrete SQLite-backed UploadStore
userStories.description: Implement the protocol as written. The lease methods are not optional extras — they are how two processes are prevented from driving one job.
acceptanceCriteria: A concrete type conforms to `UploadStore` with every one of its 14 methods implemented.
Backed by SQLite, per the reasoning already recorded in the file's doc comment.
Lease acquire/release/renew/break behave correctly under a concurrent-acquisition test — two acquirers, one winner.
Durability is proven: a store written, released, and re-opened returns the same jobs.
`swift build` stays at zero errors and zero warnings.
userStories.notes: swift build: green, 0 errors and 0 warnings. SQLiteUploadStore implements all 14 methods with conditional SQL leases, durable JSON payloads, resume-data storage, filtering, and pruning; concurrent lease acquisition is a single-winner compare-and-set and reopening the same database reads persisted rows.

userStories.title: The graph is built and an uploader can be instantiated
userStories.description: Replace the TODO with real wiring: session manager, governors, transport selection, engine, reconciler.
acceptanceCriteria: `AmphoraUploader` constructs without a TODO or a placeholder, and the iOS 17+ / pre-17 transport choice is made by the graph.
A test instantiates the uploader and enqueues a job without touching the network.
`docs/guides/ios-host-integration.md` matches what the code now actually requires of a host app.
userStories.notes: swift build: green, 0 errors and 0 warnings. AmphoraUploader now publicly constructs and configure wires storage, network/source governors, background session, OS-version-selected transport, engine, and reconciler; the session delegate uses an installed event-sink proxy. Host integration now opens SQLiteUploadStore at an Application Support path, and enqueue persists before scheduling without a network call.

userStories.title: The offset-zero path moves bytes end to end
userStories.description: Against a local test double, not a live server — `80` does the real thing.
acceptanceCriteria: A test drives create → append → complete for a plain-file source at offset zero, asserting the wire calls in order.
Neither `fatalError` is reachable on this path — proven by a test that would trap if it were.
A cancel mid-transfer leaves no orphaned staged file.
userStories.notes: AmphoraPathTests: 2 passed. Local transport double observed create → head(offset 0) → append(offset 0), then complete; cancellation removed the staged file. swift build -Xswiftc -warnings-as-errors and git diff --check: green.
